topics.label: Lecture framing and introduction to cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the lecture’s aims and its framework for connecting cancer mutations to functional hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth and survival signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer alters normal cell maturation, using hematological cancers and intestinal epithelium to show the resulting changes.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of p53 signaling and the balance of mitochondrial apoptotic regulators allows cancer cells to evade death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and growth-limiting stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the safeguards that restrict continued cell proliferation and consolidate how cancer bypasses them to sustain growth.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how altered metabolism supports cancer and feeds back into the mechanisms driving its development.

topics.label: Angiogenesis and tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why tumors require a switch toward blood-vessel formation to grow beyond the limits of oxygen and nutrient diffusion.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells spread to distant sites and what determines whether that dissemination produces a detectable secondary tumor.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by revisiting its central message, recommending further reading and inviting questions.
